findings.title: KeyError when Integration metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the re-install path does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The `sender` metadata is only populated in build_integration when the webhook-provided state contains `sender` (see `if state.get("sender")` in build_integration). Integrations created before this change, or where the installation webhook never arrived/was processed, will have no `sender` key in metadata, so any re-install/repair attempt for such an integration raises an uncaught KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the friendly error page. The lookup should use `.get("sender", {})` style access and treat a missing sender as a failed verification (or fall back gracefully).

findings.title: Token exchange HTTP errors are not handled
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is called outside the try/except that wraps safe_urlread. If GitHub's token endpoint is unreachable or returns an error status, safe_urlopen raises and the user gets a 500 rather than the intended 'Invalid installation request' error page. Similarly, `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an API call that can raise ApiError (e.g. GitHub outage), which is also uncaught. Both calls should be guarded so the pipeline fails with the rendered error response instead of an exception.

findings.title: Sender check is bypassed on fresh installs
findings.body: The authenticated-user-vs-installer verification only runs in the branch where an Integration row already exists without an OrganizationIntegration. In the fresh-install path (`except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()`), the github_authenticated_user captured during OAuth is never compared to the account that installed the app. A user who is logged into Sentry but authenticated to GitHub as a different account can complete an installation of a GitHub App installed by someone else (e.g. an org app installed by another org member is fine, but any GitHub user who can see the installation_id can attach an app installation they don't own to their Sentry org). If the intent stated in the PR description ('fail if there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user and the user who installed the GitHub app') is to be enforced, the comparison must also be made on the fresh-install path, e.g. by comparing against the installation's account/sender from get_installation_info.
